title: Kernel orchestra switchover replay: multiworkload quant tradeoffs
body:
Summary:

This note documents an exploratory sweep we ran to understand how dynamic kernel switchover heuristics interact with quantization formats (INT8, AWQ, GPTQ, FP8) across mixed workloads. The goal was to replicate multiworkload burst patterns using a deterministic replay harness and measure both performance (p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization) and quality regressions (perplexity delta on validation corpus and a small NLU probe).

Why this is different:
- Instead of a single-model/static-benchmark approach, we replay realistic mixed traffic (chat+completion+embedding proxies) to surface transient switchover pathology.
- We instrumented the kernel scheduler to capture switch events and queue depth when switching between CUTLASS/CUBLAS/triton/custom-vector kernels.
- We included a short-lived RL-style decision policy prototype that prefers lower p99 over raw throughput under high tail jitter.

Testbed configuration:
- Models: Llama-2-13B (float baseline), Redwood-Tiny-7B-v1 (production surrogate), Mistral-7B (capacity probe).
- Quant methods: INT8 symmetric, GPTQ (8-bit post-hoc), AWQ (per-channel asymmetric), FP8 (E4M3 profile).
- Hardware: NVIDIA H100-80GB SXM (primary), NVIDIA A100-80GB PCIe (secondary).
- Kernels: CUTLASS matmul kernels, Triton-fused attention kernels, cuBLAS fallback, custom-vector (tile 128x64) low-precision kernel developed in PR #4123.
- Workload: replay of 12h production trace compressed to 30m synthetic run. Mix: 60% short-chat (<=32 tokens), 30% completion (<=512 tokens), 10% long-context (>=1024 tokens). Burst pattern: 5m normal, 30s burst @ 3x QPS, repeating.
- Batching: dynamic batching with max batch 32, latency SLOs configured at 200ms p99 for short-chat, 1200ms p99 for completions.
- KV cache warm/cold runs included.

Methodology:
1) For each quant/kernel combination we ran three full replays: cold-kv, warm-kv steady, warm-kv burst.
2) Logged events: kernel-enter/kernel-exit, queue-depth, scheduling-latency, memory-copy overhead, CUDA-stream stalls.
3) Quality checks: running perplexity on heldout 2k-sample assistant-style prompts and running an NLU micro-eval (6-shot intent detection probe).
4) Performed A/B with RL-policy enabled vs baseline greedy throughput policy.

Key observations (high level):
- AWQ on H100 delivered the highest sustained tokens/sec for Llama-2-13B in steady state ("throughput leader"), but showed elevated p99 jitter during bursts because the AWQ-optimized custom kernel occasionally triggered a fallback to cuBLAS for a small set of attention shapes, causing a 1.8x latency spike for those requests.
- GPTQ preserved quality better than AWQ across all models on both hardware types (perplexity delta median: AWQ +0.9, GPTQ +0.2 relative to float). However GPTQ variants consistently used slightly different kernel paths on A100 which negatively affected throughput (~12% lower tokens/sec) because cuBLAS pathways could not be fused with our vector tile kernel.
- FP8 (E4M3) reduced memory footprint by ~28% vs INT8 in our builds (due to packing/alignment efficiencies) but increased small-sample noise: short-chat p50 was similar to INT8 but p99 regressed by ~15% in cold-KV runs. FP8 on H100 benefitted from float-accumulate optimizations giving better throughput than FP8 on A100.
- INT8 symmetric was the most stable across kernel switchover events (fewest fallbacks) but ended up with slightly worse quality on assistant-style prompts (perplexity delta ~+1.7).
- Custom-vector kernel reduced p99 by 18% during long-context workloads compared to Triton fused kernels, owing to reduced kernel-launch overhead and tiling that better amortized memory reads. But it required a small prefetch change to avoid L2 thrash.
- The RL-style policy that trades throughput for p99 (switching kernels proactively when queue depth > threshold) improved p99 by ~22% at the cost of ~9% throughput during bursts. It prevented the large fallbacks we saw with AWQ during shape outliers.

Representative numbers (Llama-2-13B on H100, warm-KV, steady):
- AWQ + custom-vector: p50 18ms, p95 62ms, p99 210ms, tokens/sec 48k
- GPTQ + CUTLASS: p50 20ms, p95 75ms, p99 260ms, tokens/sec 42k
- INT8 + cuBLAS fallback: p50 22ms, p95 68ms, p99 230ms, tokens/sec 38k
- FP8 + Triton: p50 19ms, p95 80ms, p99 270ms, tokens/sec 44k

Representative numbers (burst window, same setup):
- AWQ + custom-vector: p99 spikes to 420ms (fallback events), tokens/sec drops to 28k for 8s windows
- GPTQ + CUTLASS: p99 stable 300ms, tokens/sec 34k steady
- RL-policy (AWQ): p99 capped at 180ms, tokens/sec average 43k

Quality results:
- Perplexity on assistant probe (lower is better, relative to float baseline): AWQ +0.9, GPTQ +0.2, INT8 +1.7, FP8 +1.4.
- NLU probe accuracy delta (relative to float): AWQ -1.1%, GPTQ -0.3%, INT8 -2.8%, FP8 -1.9%.

Failure modes observed:
- Shape outliers (attention window sizes that were uncommon in training) triggered kernel mismatches which then caused a heavy fallback path into cuBLAS; these fallbacks serialized requests causing tail latency amplification.
- Memory alignment differences for FP8 caused occasional small memcpy penalties on A100 with PCIe configuration (didn't reproduce on SXM).
- Dynamic batching heuristics sometimes grouped long-context requests with short-chat requests leading to amplification of latency for the short requests; this was exacerbated on kernels with poor launch amortization.

Operational suggestions and mitigations:
- Add a shape-classification fast-path: at admission time classify request into a shape bucket and prefer kernels that are known-stable for that bucket. This reduces outlier fallbacks.
- Introduce a lightweight kernel-health probe that runs a small micro-batch on new kernel variants during low traffic and marks unstable kernels as experimental.
- Expose an SLO-driven policy toggle in runtime: when p99 approaches SLO, bias routing toward kernels with historically low tail even if throughput decreases (~10% throttle).
- Prefetch L2 lines for custom-vector kernels on H100 to avoid L2 thrash; small change in allocator + prefetch reduced p99 by ~12% in long-context runs.
- For AWQ, add a tiny compatibility shim to convert edge attention shapes into fused-friendly shapes when possible; this avoids the cuBLAS fallback for many cases.

Immediate follow-ups (next 2 sprints):
- SRV-9901: Implement admission-time shape bucket classifier and test on 48h production replay (owner: Ava)
- PR 4217: small prefetch/allocator change for custom-vector kernel (owner: Liam)
- Experiment: run FP8 pack alignment variant on A100 PCIe vs SXM and file hardware-specific tuning knobs (owner: Sofia)
- Investigate: automated kernel canary rollout with circuit-breaker for fallback rate > X% during 5m window.

Notes for product/ops:
- Customer-facing impact: customers running mixed chat/completion workloads on AWQ may see occasional user-facing latency blips during bursts. Recommend showcasing RL-policy and kernel-health canary as options for Dedicated customers with high tail sensitivity.
- Cost note: AWQ throughput advantage on H100 can translate to ~18-25% cost savings on token-unit compute for steady usage but that gain is reduced for bursty workloads where fallbacks occur.

Appendix (short):
- Harness used: replay harness v2.3 (github link above).
- Metrics pipeline: prometheus + per-request traces to trace-store; p99 numbers are request-side observed latencies (includes serialization + copy).
- Raw logs and event traces archived under: gs://redwood-fieldlab/kernel-orchestra/mar2029/ (linked in PR).

This doc is a working note. Please leave comments in the PR or slack thread referenced above. If we agree on the mitigations, I'll open matching Jira tickets and a short runbook for on-call to triage kernel-fallback incidents.
